title: MOCK: How a WhatsApp call travels

turns.text: Every WhatsApp call feels instant. What really happens when you tap call?
First comes signaling. Both phones exchange small setup messages and agree to talk.
Fine, but my voice is not a text message. How does sound travel?
A codec compresses your voice and chops it into tiny packets.
So who can listen to those packets?
They are end to end encrypted, so even relay servers cannot read them.
Relay servers? I thought calls went straight from phone to phone.
Sometimes they do. When a network blocks that path, a relay forwards the encrypted packets.
What happens when my connection gets worse mid call?
The app adapts. It lowers the bitrate and smooths over lost packets.
Signaling, encrypted packets, and smart adaptation. The exact infrastructure details stay private.
